title: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science - Pre Vocational Studies - Agricultural Practices
exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: The first pre-planting operation a farmer must carry out when setting up a new farm is the ________.
questions.explain: The choice of site is the very first step in farming because selecting a suitable piece of land with the right soil type, topography, and accessibility is crucial for agricultural success.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: In pre-planting operations, the removal of vegetation, bushes, and shrubs from the chosen farm site is known as ________.
questions.explain: Clearing (or slashing) is the process of cutting down the natural vegetation and bushes on the land to prepare it for subsequent operations.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: The pre-planting operation that involves digging out the remaining roots and base of cut trees to prevent regrowth and ease machinery movement is called ________.
questions.explain: Stumping refers to the complete uprooting and removal of tree stumps and their root systems from the cleared farmland.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: The practice of marking out the farmland to ensure proper layout and optimal use of the land area before planting is called ________.
questions.explain: Plotting or laying out involves dividing the farm land into sections for different crops, roads, and farm structures.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Tilling, which encompasses plowing and harrowing, is a pre-planting operation primarily done to ________.
options: Harden the soil for the roots
Protect the farm from wild animals
Loosen the soil and improve aeration
questions.explain: Tilling breaks up the hard topsoil, overturning and loosening it. This improves soil aeration, water infiltration, and creates a soft seedbed for planting.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: A specialized plot or structure where tiny, delicate seeds are initially planted and nurtured until they are strong enough to be transplanted to the main field is called a ________.
questions.explain: A nursery provides intensive care and a favorable environment for germinating delicate seeds (like tomatoes and cocoa) into strong seedlings before transplanting.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Before planting, seeds are sometimes coated with protective chemicals like fungicides and insecticides. This planting operation is known as ________.
questions.explain: Seed treatment (or seed dressing) is the application of chemicals to seeds before planting to protect them from soil-borne diseases and pests.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: The post-planting operation of removing weak or excess seedlings from a stand to prevent overcrowding and reduce competition is known as ________.
questions.explain: Thinning is done by uprooting the weakest seedlings in an overcrowded spot, leaving only the healthiest and giving them enough space and nutrients to grow.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Which post-planting practice involves planting new seeds or seedlings in spots where the previously planted ones failed to germinate or died?
questions.explain: Supplying (also called 'filling-in' or 'beating up') is the replacement of seeds that failed to sprout or died shortly after emergence, ensuring the farm maintains an optimal plant population.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
